title: The Almond Yogurt Study (AYS)
official: The Impact of Almond Food Structure in a Standardized Yogurt Breakfast Meal on Gastric Emptying, Oral Processing Behaviours, Appetite-Regulating Hormones, Postprandial Metabolism, and Subjective Satiety: A Randomized Crossover Trial
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to explore how almond food structure influences gastric emptying rates when consumed by healthy adult women as part of a standardized breakfast meal. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the structure of almonds (whole, chopped, buttered) influence gastric emptying ?
* What is the correlation between chewing behaviour, gastric emptying, and changes in postprandial triacylglycerols and satiety (hormones and ratings) within the context of an increasingly disrupted nut matrix.
conditions: This Study Explores the Relationships Between Almond Particle Size, Chewing, Gastric Emptying, and Postprandial Metabolism
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Healthy female adults aged 18-45 years.
* Body Mass Index (BMI) between 18.5-27.9 kg/m2, or waist circumference of less than 88 cm
* Visible gastric antrum on ultrasound
* No known food allergies or sensitivities
* Non restrained eaters (TFEQ, see below)
* No history of gastrointestinal diseases that may interfere with eating behavior or digestion
* Not on medications that affect appetite (including GLP-1 agonists), digestion, blood sugar regulation, saliva production, or chewing
* Stable medication use
* Non-smokers
* Not gained or lost significant weight during the past 3 months
* Regular monthly menstrual cycles
* Not pregnant, lactating or post-menopausal

Exclusion Criteria:

* Diabetes or other metabolic disorders affecting glycemia and overall cardiometabolic health
* Blood pressure \> 140/90 mm Hg
* Any food allergies, intolerances, or sensitivities
* Pregnant or breastfeeding
* Participation in another clinical trial
* Excessive alcohol consumption (more than 14 drinks per week)
* Smokers or those with a smoking history of more than 10 years
* Regular use of recreational drugs (e.g., marijuana, ecstasy, LSD, magic mushrooms, etc.)
* Restrained eater (\>16) as defined by the questionnaire at screening (Three-Factor Eating Questionnaire, Stunkard et al., 1985)
* Unusual sleep patterns
* Irregular breakfast consumption
* Recent weight changes, or intended weight loss or gain; lost/gained 10% of body weight within the last 6 months
* Food allergies/sensitivities or any life-threatening allergies
* Using medications known to affect appetite, digestion, blood sugar regulation, or chewing/swallowing (excluding oral contraceptives).
* Experiences dry mouth in general or due to medication side effects
* Inability to adhere to study protocols
* Not comfortable providing IV-line blood samples
* Not comfortable providing ultrasound scans
* Not comfortable being video recorded while eating
* Avoids consuming almonds/yogurt in general
* Avoids eating hard foods to prevent dental fractures
